question_text: A 64-year-old woman comes to the physician because of worsening intermittent nausea and burning pain in her upper abdomen for 4 hours. She has not had retrosternal chest pain, shortness of breathing, or vomiting. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years. Her only medications are lisinopril and insulin. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 155/75 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft, with mild tenderness to palpation of the epigastrium but no guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. An ECG is shown. This patient's current condition is most likely to cause which of the following findings on cardiac examination?
